note.question: How long should the retailer hold the consumer’s orders before sending them to a third-party logistics provider (3PL) for processing?
note.overview: A significant percentage of online consumers place consecutive orders within a short duration. To reduce the total order arrangement cost, an online retailer may consolidate consecutive orders from the same consumer. We investigate how long the retailer should hold the consumer’s orders before sending them to a third-party logistics provider (3PL) for processing.

source.quote: To model the transitions among the single-dimensional MDPs, we introduce a choice model to characterize a consumer’s sequential decision process after placing an order.
After placing an order, the consumer has the following three options: (i) dwell on the platform to search fur­ ther, (ii) leave the system immediately, or (iii) place another order.
Each network is associated with the order features xl of the past consecutive orders placed by the consumer in the consumer’s shopping journey.

We define a directed network Nxl = (Vxl ∪{n,M},Axl) to model this sequential decision process, where Vxl represents a set of nodes, n repre­ sents the option of leaving the system immediately, M represents the option of placing another order, and Axl represents a set of arcs.
Spe­ cifically, from the current node (xl,w), the utility of choosing node k consists of a deterministic term u(xl,w),k and a random error term ˜ɛ(xl,w),k.
